query: In powder-vapourization (MoO3 + sulfur) CVD growth of monolayer MoS2, what do published experiments report about how substrate position or distance from the MoO3 boat (or MoO3 boat temperature or amount) changes domain size, nucleation density, shape or Mo:S-related morphology? Give each study with DOI, the values compared, the direction and size of the effect, and whether only that variable changed. Prefer open-access papers.
answer:
## Powder-source CVD: reported comparisons

**The clearest controlled result is non-monotonic:** increasing the MoO₃-zone temperature from 1073 to 1098 K increased monolayer-triangle side length from approximately 30 to 100 µm, but increasing it again to 1123 K produced more, smaller, overlapping or multilayer crystals. Distance and position results are less readily reduced to one rule: moving across a substrate changes both precursor delivery and the local growth environment. Here, *domain size* denotes an individual crystal unless the study explicitly reports a continuous-film dimension. (jian2019structureandproperties pages 5-7, xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6)

| Study and DOI | Values compared; reported effect | Did only the stated variable change? |
|---|---|---|
| **Jian, Chang & Xu, 2019**, open access, **10.3390/ma12020198** | At a nominal **5 cm MoO₃-source–substrate separation**, with the sulfur zone held at **453 K**, MoO₃-zone temperatures of **1048, 1073, 1098 and 1123 K** gave, respectively, almost no deposit; monolayer triangles of approximately **30 µm side length**; independent monolayer triangles of approximately **100 µm** (**~3.3-fold larger** than at 1073 K); and **more numerous but smaller**, touching/stacked, partly multilayer deposits. No numerical nucleation densities were reported. (jian2019structureandproperties pages 1-3, jian2019structureandproperties pages 5-7) | **Temperature was the intended variable in this series**, with 20 mg MoO₃, a 30-min hold and stated 100-sccm flow; however, the substrate was only **4–5.5 cm** from the Mo source in the temperature-series description, and its temperature is not independently held fixed as the nearby source zone changes. Separately, **simultaneous** S/MoO₃ heating gave MoO₂-rich particles or quadrilaterals, whereas starting S heating after the MoO₃ zone reached **837 K** yielded cleaner triangles: heating *sequence*, not just final source temperature, changed. (jian2019structureandproperties pages 1-3, jian2019structureandproperties pages 3-5, jian2019structureandproperties pages 5-7) |
| **Momeni et al., 2018**, open access, **10.1038/s41699-018-0072-4** | With **2 mg MoO₃ placed 0.5 cm upstream** of a face-down substrate and **200 mg S approximately 15 cm upstream**, microscopy across the substrate at **0.4-cm intervals** found approximately **10-µm hexagons at the leading position**, followed by quasi-hexagons and then triangles at later positions. The leading/high-supply region showed greater coverage and denser nucleation; other regions had more widely spaced islands. Growth at **800 and 725 °C** was examined, but the retrieved text does **not** give a defensible numerical size or density change between those temperatures or at every position. (momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 6-7, momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 5-6, momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 3-5, momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 2-3) | **Within a growth run, sampling position changed**, not loaded powder mass; position also entails a precursor-concentration/deposition gradient. **Between runs**, the MoO₃/substrate-zone growth temperature changed, so the temperature comparison is not a source-temperature-only test at fixed substrate temperature. (momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 6-7, momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 5-6) |
| **Xu et al., 2018**, open access, **10.3390/ma11060870** | This is a useful **within-substrate position**, *not* a calibrated longitudinal distance-from-boat, comparison. At a fixed location along gas flow, moving **across** the substrate from **x = 0.1 to 1, 1.5 and 2.5 mm** changed deposits from nuclei to triangles/darts of up to **7 µm**, triangles of about **15 µm**, and partially joined triangles exceeding **20 µm**. A central band at **x ≈ 3.5–13.5 mm** became continuous film; farther across it grew sparse again. Five equal-area regions yielded effective nucleation densities of **0.0103, 0.0167, 0.0389, 0.0302 and 0.0036 µm⁻²**, respectively: central section 3 was approximately **10.8 times** section 5. The paper describes an inferred spatial Mo:S/supply gradient, **not a measured Mo:S composition map**. Its triangles can also have **monolayer interiors and few-layer edges**. (xu2018controlofthe pages 1-3, xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8) | **Yes for comparing locations in that run:** nominal loads were **0.1 mg MoO₃**, distributed under four face-down substrates, and **10 mg S**, with precursor boats **24 cm apart**. But location changes the local gas-flow/precursor environment; the reported millimetres are **transverse substrate coordinates**, not distance from the MoO₃ boat. A *separate* carrier-flow series changed **10 to 280 sccm**, so its density changes must not be attributed to position. (xu2018controlofthe pages 1-3, xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8) |
| **Sitek et al., 2020**, **10.1021/acsami.0c06173** | Standard conditions put substrates **10 cm from the Mo precursor**, approximately **8 mm above the tube bottom**, with **50 mg MoO₃ at 687 ± 15 °C**, substrate **770 °C**, and **125 mg S**. On **SiO₂**, changing growth conditions yielded circular, higher-coverage and truncated-triangular morphologies; on **graphene**, domains remained predominantly triangular, with only slight reported changes in grain size/density. Bringing substrates **“significantly closer”** to the precursors enabled a continuous film on graphene, but **neither the new distance nor a numerical size/density effect is given**. (sitek2020substrateinducedvariancesin pages 4-7, sitek2020substrateinducedvariancesin pages 7-12, sitek2020substrateinducedvariancesin pages 15-18) | **Not a quantified distance-only experiment.** Its illustrated comparisons separately include growth time **15 → 60 min**, substrate temperature **770 → 900 °C**, and an approximately **20-fold S-flux increase** achieved by changing *both* sulfur mass (**125 → 1000 mg**) and sulfur temperature (**115 → 180 °C**). Substrate material is itself another comparison. These should not be represented as effects of changing MoO₃ mass or source temperature alone. (sitek2020substrateinducedvariancesin pages 4-7, sitek2020substrateinducedvariancesin pages 7-12) |
| **Lara Saenz et al., 2016**, **10.1557/adv.2016.484** | Moving the **sulfur boat**, rather than the substrate or MoO₃ boat, from **36 to 17 cm from the furnace centre/MoO₃ position** changed predominantly rhomboidal **MoO₂/MoS₂** deposits to triangular **monolayer MoS₂**. Both recipes loaded **0.4 g MoO₃ and 0.8 g S** and reached **850 °C for 15 min**; no comparable individual-domain sizes or densities were supplied. (saenz2016effectsofsynthesis pages 4-6) | **No:** the heating ramp also changed from **15 °C min⁻¹** to a **17.6 °C min⁻¹** ramp to 550 °C followed by **5 °C min⁻¹** to 850 °C. This is evidence about sulfur timing/placement and reaction route, **not** an isolated substrate–MoO₃-distance effect. (saenz2016effectsofsynthesis pages 4-6) |
| **Tummala et al., 2022**, open access, **10.3390/nano12060973** | Flat-growth conditions used **1 mg MoO₃, 200 mg S, a 750 °C MoO₃ zone and PTAS-treated substrate face-down above its crucible**. Without PTAS, isolated lateral domains were **<10 µm**; under the promoted recipe triangles merged into continuous monolayer regions **>200 µm** across—**film extent, not a >200-µm single-crystal size**. A modified recipe produced *vertically aligned bulk/few-layer* nanosheets, rather than the flat monolayer. (tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 2-3, tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 3-5, tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 5-7) | **No for the flat–vertical comparison:** sulfur loading changed **200 → 300 mg**, PTAS was omitted, and sulfur introduction/boat movement and gas-flow history changed. Lower MoO₃-zone temperatures used on **TaN** involved a **different substrate and flows**; they do not isolate a temperature effect on monolayer domain size. No numerical substrate–MoO₃ distance or nucleation-density comparison is reported. (tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 2-3, tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 3-5, tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 5-7, tummala2022ambientpressurechemical pages 7-9) |
| **Torrel, 2017 dissertation**, open access, **10.7282/t39026x7** | A positional XPS comparison of powder-grown deposits gave mean **S:Mo = 2.33** at an upper position versus **0.72** at a lower one (**~3.2-fold**); upper samples averaged **35% higher S:Mo**. Within-position readings millimetres apart could span **2.15–3.64** or **0.2–0.8**. Moving MoO₃ to a cooler furnace region improved deposition homogeneity but not film quality/reproducibility. These are **composition/film observations**, not quantified monolayer domain-size or nucleation-density results. (torrel2017chemicalvapordeposition pages 82-87, torrel2017chemicalvapordeposition pages 76-82) | **Not distance alone:** arrangements included different heights and orientations, and sulfur-source temperatures of **170, 190 and 210 °C** were studied. The account says stoichiometry depended less on horizontal Mo-source distance than on sulfur temperature and vertical position; source relocation also changes temperature and delivery. XPS ratios must not be interpreted as measured stoichiometry of individual monolayer flakes. (torrel2017chemicalvapordeposition pages 76-82, torrel2017chemicalvapordeposition pages 82-87) |

**Interpretation and limits.** These studies support a local-supply picture rather than “farther always means larger”: inadequate Mo delivery can leave no crystals or small isolated islands; intermediate delivery can enlarge monolayer triangles; still greater effective delivery can increase nucleation/coalescence and multilayer growth. The **~30 → ~100 µm → smaller/multilayer** source-temperature series is the strongest numerical example, while the transverse-position and substrate-gradient studies show why precursor flux and local environment matter. None establishes a universal conversion from centimetres away from a particular MoO₃ boat to domain size in another reactor. (jian2019structureandproperties pages 5-7, xu2018controlofthe pages 3-6, xu2018controlofthe pages 6-8, momeni2018multiscaleframeworkfor pages 3-5)

**Scope warning:** A source–substrate spacing quoted as part of a recipe is not itself evidence that spacing was varied. Also, increased **sulfur powder** in a recent monolayer-circle study (**350–450 mg S** at fixed **6 mg MoO₃**) enlarged circles, with a reported maximum around **250 µm**; that is a sulfur-dose result and is **not** a MoO₃-amount comparison. Its published DOI is **10.1021/acs.cgd.6c00071**; the examined open manuscript has DOI **10.48550/arXiv.2601.01463**. (patra2601spontaneousgrowthof pages 1-2, patra2601spontaneousgrowthof pages 2-3)
